hook: I spent $89.72 to make my shower feel like a hotel

scenes.visual_prompt: Flat lay of three products — handheld showerhead, squeegee, folded towels — each with a visible price tag
scenes.voiceover: Three things, eighty-nine dollars and seventy-two cents total.

scenes.visual_prompt: Handheld showerhead spraying strong water, $29.94 price label visible
scenes.voiceover: The showerhead fixes the pressure — eight modes, scale-resistant nozzles.

scenes.visual_prompt: Squeegee hanging directly on the shower arm by its built-in hook, no suction cup, then being pulled across glass
scenes.voiceover: More pressure means more water hitting the glass, so this squeegee hangs by a built-in hook — no suction cup to fall off.

scenes.visual_prompt: Close-up of thick folded towels, texture visible, 600 GSM label graphic overlay
scenes.voiceover: And the towels are 600 GSM Turkish cotton — hotel sets run that dense, house sets usually run 300 to 400.

scenes.visual_prompt: Wide shot of a steamy bathroom, clean glass, person wrapped in a thick towel after a shower
scenes.on_screen_text: 79,026 ratings — the biggest sample on this list
scenes.voiceover: That's the biggest review sample of anything I've tried this year.

scenes.visual_prompt: Final flat lay with a total price graphic reading '$89.72 total'
scenes.voiceover: Less than one nice dinner out, for a shower that doesn't feel like a rental anymore.

caption: The $89.72 shower upgrade: pressure, glass, and towels — all three linked in bio, each one picked for a reason.
